BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r5.claim: He calls them to fear punishment and obey him in the truth he commands.
BURSEVI:v6p213#3/r5.anchor: خافوا من عقابه {وأطيعون} فيما آمركم به من الحق.

STUDYQURAN:26:123/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:123/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:123/r1.claim: The five opening verses of Hūd's story follow the same pattern as Noah's and the stories of later prophets.
STUDYQURAN:26:123/r1.anchor: These five verses form a pattern that opens the story of Noah and each of the prophets who follow

TAB-FULL:v17p606#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p606#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p606#2/r3.claim: Fearing God means obeying Him and following His commands and prohibitions; obeying Hūd means heeding this call and warning.
TAB-FULL:v17p606#2/r3.anchor: {فاتقوا الله} [آل عمران: 50] بطاعته والانتهاء إلى ما يأمركم وينهاكم {وأطيعون} [آل عمران: 50] فيما آمركم به من اتقاء الله

TABATABAI:26:123-130/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r1.claim: The story concerns Hud and ʿAd; as in Noah's story, the people are called deniers of the messengers although they outwardly rejected only one.
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r1.anchor: بيان تشير الآيات إلى قصة هود عليه السلام وقومه وهم قوم عاد

TABATABAI:26:123-130/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r5.claim: Some exegetes say these stories stress that the prophets are trustworthy, seek no wage, and command piety and obedience to show their shared mission of true knowledge and conduct leading to reward and away from punishment, despite differences in detailed laws across eras.
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن تصدير هذه القصص الخمس بذكر أمانة الرسل وعدم سؤالهم أجرا

TABATABAI:26:123-130/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r6.claim: The repeated ending of all seven stories shows that most peoples turn away from God's signs; God is mighty in requiting deniers and merciful in saving believers, as explained in the surah's purpose.
TABATABAI:26:123-130/r6.anchor: ونظيره الكلام في ختم جميع القصص السبع الموردة في السورة بقوله { إن في ذلك لآية

TABATABAI:26:126/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:126/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:126/r1.claim: The command to fear God and obey follows their excess in both appetite and anger and their departure from servitude; they should abandon indulgence and arrogance.
TABATABAI:26:126/r1.anchor: ومحصل الآيات الثلاث أنكم مسرفون في جانبي الشهوة والغضب

ELMALILI:26:123-140/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:123-140/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:123-140/r2.claim: He urges them to fear God and obey him.
ELMALILI:26:123-140/r2.anchor: Gelin Allah’tan korkun ve bana itaat edin (126).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:126/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:126/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:126/r1.claim: The command is rendered as avoiding disobedience to God and obeying Hud.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:126/r1.anchor: Artık Allah’a karşı gelmekten sakının ve bana itaat edin

SULAMI:v2p80#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p80#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p80#4/r1.claim: God-consciousness has no final limit; it is both the first and last station, and its true reality is guarding oneself even from one's own piety.
SULAMI:v2p80#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : التقوى أوائل المنازل ، وأواخرها ولا غاية له وذلك أنه ليس للمتقي غاية ينتهي إليها ،

SULAMI:v2p80#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p80#4/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p80#4/r2.claim: God-consciousness means leaving everything blameworthy and turning toward everything praiseworthy.
SULAMI:v2p80#4/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : التقوى هي التخلي من كل مذموم ، والإقبال إلى كل محمود .

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p430/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p430/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p430/r3.claim: Where the previous sūrah detailed Moses and Noah but briefly mentioned intervening nations, this sūrah details those nations’ dealings with their messengers and their fates in historical order, ending each account with a refrain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p430/r3.anchor: The sequence adopted is historical and at the end of every anecdote the repetitive verses occur.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p431/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p431/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p431/r3.claim: Hud’s repeated exhortation to fear God and obey him also rebukes people who evade his call and will not even listen.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p431/r3.anchor: Moreover, it also carries rebuke for those

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p433/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p433/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p433/r1.claim: The recurring prophetic appeal is an earnest, affectionate final warning: the people still have time to abandon wrongdoing and follow their messenger rather than corrupt leaders.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p433/r1.anchor: These words serve to remind and caution the nation in a very earnest and affectionate way in the last phase.

NASHR:v2p336/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p336/r10.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p336/r10.claim: Yaqub affirms the sixteen listed extra yāʾs in both connected and pause forms: the eight quoted forms plus أطيعون in eight places.
NASHR:v2p336/r10.anchor: أثبت الياء في جميعها يعقوب في الحالين

QIRAAT-ER:26:126:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:26:126:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:26:126:5#1/r1.claim: The full first-person yāʾ makes the I phonetically prominent through a longer final syllable, with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:26:126:5#1/r1.anchor: Full yāʾ al-mutakallim explicitly written — no semantic change but prosodic lengthening of final syllable

ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r1.claim: The five prophetic narratives repeat the call to piety, obedience, and no wage to show that missions call people to truth and saving obedience; prophets shared this aim despite differing subsidiary laws and had no worldly ambition.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r1.anchor: وحكاية الأمر بالتقوى والاطاعة ونفي سؤال الأجر في القصص الخمس وتصديرها بذلك للتنبيه على ان مبنى البعثة هو الدعاء إلى معرفة الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r2.claim: The Moses and Abraham narratives may vary the formula for stylistic variety while including other signs of the same meaning; another view says their matters were more important.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r2.anchor: ولعله لم يسلك هدا المسلك في قصتي موسى وابراهيم عليهما السلام تفننا مع ذكر ما يشعر بذلك وقيل : ان ما ذكر ثمة أهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r3.claim: The account places the lands of عاد between Oman and Hadramawt and describes them as fertile and populous before God turned them into wilderness and dunes.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p109#7/r3.anchor: وكانت منازل عاد بين عمان وحضرموت وكانت أخصب البلاد وأعمرها فجعلها الله تعالى مفاوز ورمالا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p122/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p122/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p122/r10.claim: Hud calls his people to fear God and obey him.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r11.claim: Hud concludes that his message requires them to fear God and obey him in all that he commands concerning steadfast reverence.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p376#2/r11.anchor: الذي هو أعظم من كل شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p164#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p164#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p164#2/r6.claim: Hud’s command follows from his appeal just as it does in Noah’s story; the yāʾ of أطيعون is omitted for the verse ending, as in Noah’s and Abraham’s accounts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p164#2/r6.anchor: عليه كما تقدم في قصة نوح

MUQATIL:26:123-131/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:123-131/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:123-131/r4.claim: “Fear God” means worship God; Hud calls them to obey his counsel.
MUQATIL:26:123-131/r4.anchor: يعنى فاعبدوا الله، { وأطيعون } [آية: 126] فيما آمركم به من النصيحة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p192#15/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p192#15/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p192#15/r1.claim: Hud calls his people to fear God by not rejecting the trustworthy messenger.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p192#15/r1.anchor: فاتقوا الله ﴾ في تكذيب الرسول الأمين

QURTUBI-FULL:26:123-129/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:123-129/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:123-129/r4.claim: Hud’s command to fear God and obey him repeats the meaning explained earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:123-129/r4.anchor: بين المعنى وقد تقدم. قوله تعالى: { أتبنون بكل ريع آية تعبثون }
